sections.heading: Introduction
paras: If roles are Scrum's who, backlogs and events are its what and when. The 2022 midterm gave this cluster 10 of its 25 agile marks (Q4.3 on backlogs+sprints, Q4.4 on planning and review meetings), so precision about purpose, timing and participants pays directly.

sections.heading: The two backlogs
paras: The Product Backlog is the single ordered list of everything that might go into the product — features, fixes, knowledge work — owned and ordered by the Product Owner, evolving as requirements change. The Sprint Backlog is the Developers' plan for one sprint: the Sprint Goal (why), the selected Product Backlog items (what), and the delivery plan (how). Once the sprint starts, its backlog is the team's commitment, not a suggestion box.

paras: Note the review/retrospective split students blur: the review inspects the product with stakeholders; the retrospective inspects the process within the team. Worksheet 2's 4-week-sprint scenario puts both in the two days after the sprint — review first (what did we build?), retrospective second (how do we work better?).

summary: Product Backlog holds evolving priorities, Sprint Backlog holds one sprint's commitment; planning, dailies, review and retrospective inspect and adapt product and process in turn.
title: Backlogs, sprints and Scrum events

activities.explanation: Commit, steer, inspect the product with stakeholders, then improve the process. Review looks outward; retrospective looks inward.

activities.prompt: Which event inspects the product with stakeholders?

distractor.0: Planning commits to the goal — inspection happens at the end.
distractor.1: Dailies steer the Developers' own plan.
distractor.3: The retrospective inspects the process, within the team only.

activities.explanation: The review demos the increment to stakeholders and adapts the backlog; the retrospective follows and improves how the team works.

steps.title: 1 · Sprint planning (start)
steps.text: PO presents priorities; Developers select items and plan delivery. Output: Sprint Goal + Sprint Backlog commitment.

steps.title: 2 · Daily stand-ups
steps.text: ~15 min: what was done, what is next, blockers. Developers sync; the plan adapts.

steps.title: 3 · Sprint review (end)
steps.text: Demo the working increment to stakeholders; adapt the Product Backlog. Inspects the PRODUCT.

steps.title: 4 · Retrospective (after review)
steps.text: Team reflects on its own process and agrees improvements. Inspects the PROCESS. Then the next sprint begins.
